main_body: Flat stone paving ground patch of brick-like slabs in a running-bond pattern, 4x3 tiles; no standing volume.
top_band: none - a flat ground texture; the column scan shows only repeating mortar/stone rows (L=143 stone, 115/90 joint lines), no top-and-front structure
evidence: This is a terrain ground tile (stone paving), not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. The column scan shows a repeating pattern of stone slabs separated by joint lines with no volumetric top or front face. It is a flat top-down floor surface, appropriate for the terrain kind, with no side faces or standing structure. Nothing in it breaks the terrain contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile, against 26 for the grass reference and 80 distinct colours there. The paving reference has 7 colours per tile but 0% flat fill, while the candidate's 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 44%. The slabs are large areas of one flat tone (#9a8c80) with only a few highlight and shadow pixels at corners. The dark joint lines are 100% near-neutral, so they read as a grey/black grid rather than a tinted material tone. Slabs have no grain, speckle or per-stone shading, and the identical repeated slab pattern looks mechanical. It is much thinner than both references.
